# Visualization audit and implementation notes

## Phase 1 audit (2026-09-17, refactor starting point)

Current layout: the Vite project lived directly in `dist/visual/` root
(`package.json`/`tsconfig.json`/`vite.config.ts`/`package-lock.json` mixed with
`src/`, the built `index.html` + `assets/`, and two copies of
`release-metadata.json`). `vite.config.ts` used `build.outDir: '.'`, so the
production build overwrote its own entry (`index.html` was the built artifact);
Vite itself warns that the outDir is the project root. Frontend entry:
`src/main.tsx` → `src/App.tsx` (monolithic: pages + inspector + raw chart +
data loading in one component). Tests: `src/contract.test.ts` (vitest, 5 tests,
baseline passing). Tools: `tools/prepare-release.mjs` (release metadata from
the incumbent registry + crossfit summary), `tools/export-motion.mjs`
(TXT → motion.json/motion.bin, record format `f64_ms_6xf32_le`).

Canonical inference path (unchanged by this refactor): `src/pipeline/` →
`Predictor` (`from_bundle`, `predict_file`, `predict_folder`, `trace_file`) →
prediction contract `dist/schema/prediction.schema.json` v1.0 (events,
optional candidates/gaps/timeline with optional `series[]`). The promoted
release is `160afaf81debf1ee`; `dist/inference` is the generated standalone
runtime (raw CLI + local inference bridge `serve.py`).

ABI: the visualization consumes the prediction contract plus optional
motion telemetry (`motion.json` v1 manifest + `motion.bin` binary records,
declared raw units — typically `raw_adc`, so real orientation replay stays
gated on explicit calibration). The frontend never computes features,
candidates, verifier scores, or events.

Refactor outcome: frontend development files moved under `app/`; `src/` split
into `pages/components/motion/data/runtime/styles/tests`; the Vite entry
`app/index.html` is separate from the generated root `index.html`/`assets/`;
release metadata consolidated to `runtime/release-metadata.json` (generated by
`tools/prepare-release.mjs`). Preserved as-is: `tools/export-motion.mjs`,
telemetry record format, demo fixture, styles, Motion Replay behavior, and the
Canvas timeline. Compatibility constraints: browser folder-picker support
varies (file picker stays as fallback); real-session orientation needs
calibration; absolute wrist trajectory is never reconstructed.

## Current contracts

- `dist/schema/prediction.schema.json` v1.0 contains final `events`, optional `candidates` with `admitted`, `gaps`, and `timeline` window counts with optional per-timestamp `series[]` (macro/micro probabilities, `valid`, `gap`).
- The canonical `Predictor` already computes macro/micro window probabilities before event decoding. The raw-inference distribution emits them as optional `timeline.series`; this changes no candidates, scores, event policy, or the promoted bundle (four-way parity test covers it).
- Original `collect_data*.txt` uses millisecond timestamps, `ACC_X/Y/Z`, `GYRO_X/Y/Z`, with 44 PPG columns between timestamps and IMU. The parser passes numeric IMU values through unchanged. The README calls these raw ADC values. An external data-preparation record (outside this repository) documents the training ACC target scale as 4096 counts/g; no source in this repository establishes the watch gyroscope counts-per-deg/s or counts-per-rad/s factor, signed sensor-to-body axis transform, or handedness for a specific raw session.
- Model micro features may gravity-align windows internally. Visualization telemetry reads original IMU values and must not claim to show those transformed model features.
- Battery, live device connection, wear side, and current streaming status are absent from the prediction ABI. The UI displays offline/session state and omits unsupported device claims.

## Stack and files

React + TypeScript + Vite + Three.js. `prediction.json` remains the model contract. Optional `motion.json` v1 + `motion.bin` are visualization-only telemetry: little-endian records of one float64 timestamp (ms) and six float32 raw IMU channel values. The local inference bridge exports them from uploaded raw TXT through the canonical Python session reader (same record format as `tools/export-motion.mjs`). Binary keeps full available sample resolution; the Canvas timeline downsamples only for drawing.

## Physical and coordinate limits

- Real raw ADC can be graphed as counts. Absolute acceleration in g requires explicit ACC calibration. Gyroscope integration requires an explicit gyro conversion to rad/s, signed axis mapping, and sensor frame definition. Without these, real Motion Replay is unavailable rather than fabricated.
- Visualization-only orientation uses a deterministic complementary gravity/gyro filter for calibrated telemetry. It estimates orientation, not absolute position or independent wrist-joint motion. Yaw can drift without a magnetometer. The whole forearm/wrist/hand/watch is one rigid body.
- Internal viewer coordinates: Three.js X = arm longitudinal direction toward the hand, Y = viewer/world up, Z = depth. Synthetic demo sensor axes and sensor-to-viewer mapping are declared in its fixture. A real sensor mapping must be supplied explicitly.
